rationale: I read the complete held EO 8168 (4 FR 2415, June 14, 1939): it recites that the Agriculture Department abandoned its Sitka, Alaska experiment-station reservation, revokes the Executive order of Aug. 12, 1898, and reserves those lands for the Coast and Geodetic Survey (Commerce) as a magnetic and seismological observatory site. It is a single operative sentence with no own term and no savings clause. I read the complete held EO 8854 (6 FR 4181, Aug. 16, 1941), titled 'Revoking Executive Order No. 8168 of June 14, 1939, and Withdrawing the Land Released Thereby and Other Land ...': para. 1 orders that Executive Order No. 8168 'is hereby revoked', with no condition, exception or savings language, and para. 2 separately withdraws and reserves the same lands plus an adjoining tract for the same Survey use under the President's own authority. Para. 2 is a new reservation made by EO 8854, not a continuation of EO 8168, so the whole of EO 8168 is ended by para. 1. The catalog line 'Revoked by: EO 8854' and the empty 1989 snapshot agree, but the basis is the held acting text. D6 self-check: history lists only the EO 8854 revocation events; a text search of the held corpus finds EO 8168 named only in EO 8854, in EO 8169 and EO 8853 (copies of the same Federal Register pages) and in page indexes of unrelated volumes (OCR page-number hits), so no later order amends, revives or extends EO 8168, and no earlier ending exists in the held record. Provisional NO hypothesis only.
